key_claims: Directed evolution of a Drosophila gut microbiome produced a paraquat-resistant (PQR) microbiome.
Transplanting the PQR microbiome into Drosophila increased resistance to dietary paraquat, reduced age-related gut pathologies, and extended lifespan.
The beneficial species was identified as Lactiplantibacillus plantarum, with mutations linked to greater acetate production.
Directly feeding acetate to Drosophila extended lifespan similarly to PQR bacteria colonization.
limitations: The study was conducted in Drosophila, not humans.
The source does not specify the magnitude of lifespan extension or the exact mutations.
The source does not provide details on the safety or efficacy of this approach in other organisms.
The source does not clarify whether the effects are solely due to acetate or other factors.
what_not_to_say: The study proves that this approach works in humans.
The study identifies all mechanisms by which the microbiome affects aging.
The study shows that acetate is the only beneficial metabolite.
The study provides a ready-to-use therapeutic strategy for aging.
